page.layout: One block of running text with a marginal note in the right margin at the line "exercitium". Below it, an indented verse passage in italic. At the bottom right, a catchword.

main_text.p: nuptias, quam ad pravas libi-dines, vagam ac dissolutam venerem. Ut si aliud ullum exercitium,Euripid. in An-drom. hoc maxime in-vitet ad delinquendum. Et ideo maxime reprehenden-dum, quod nullam puellarum sinat esse honestam; cum quae sese ita nudatae exponunt, omni castitate exutae videantur. Id quod Euripides ita latine versus satis indicavit.

p.i: - - - Neque si quae cupiat, Spartiadum puellarum casta esse queat. Quae cum juvenibus deserentes domos, Nudis cruribus, & laxis peplis Cursus & palaestras non tolerabiles mihi Communes exercent.

page.notes: The verse stanza is set in italic, with its lines indented; I have kept it as one paragraph. The catchword "CAP." is printed in spaced capitals and may be the opening of the next division; I have read it as printed. The initial "Quae" is printed with a large Q and is read as "Quae".
